items.headline: Alphabet falls about 12.6% after missing on revenue and profit, wiping roughly $500B off its market value
items.why: A sharp slowdown in core search-ad growth plus negative free cash flow, while AI spending keeps rising, shows investors will no longer pay for capex without a visible return timeline.

items.headline: Microsoft beats on earnings with Azure cloud revenue up 48%
items.why: Cloud demand is still compounding at scale at one hyperscaler, so the AI-spending debate is now about who monetizes it, not whether demand exists.

items.headline: Intel drops about 23% after hours on a fourth-quarter revenue forecast of $15.0B to $16.0B, below its third-quarter $16.5B
items.why: A guide below the prior quarter shows the AI build-out is not lifting every chip name, and spread of the post-earnings selloff beyond Alphabet widens the hit to semiconductor sentiment.

items.headline: Bitcoin trades near $81,400 on Oct 28, up about 2% on the day but roughly 28% below a year earlier and about 35% below its October 2025 record of $126,198
items.why: Bitcoin is rallying only modestly while rate-hike odds rise, which keeps it a risk asset sensitive to the Fed rather than a hedge against it.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters wanting a quarter-point hike
items.why: The committee shifted from unanimous in September to a split with a hawkish tilt and called inflation elevated, so the next move being discussed is up, not down.

items.headline: Futures price roughly an 84% chance of a December hike while the 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5%
items.why: A 5% long yield alongside a likely hike tightens financial conditions directly on equity valuations, especially the long-duration tech names that just sold off.

items.headline: September PCE inflation rises to 3.6% headline and 3.1% core, while real consumer spending growth slows to 2.5% and Q3 GDP is estimated at 2.1% year over year
items.why: Inflation re-accelerating while real income growth slows to 1.0% is the stagflation-lite mix that leaves the Fed little room to cut and consumers less room to spend.

items.why: Oil this far above last year's level feeds directly into the inflation prints and fuel costs behind the Fed's hawkish turn.

items.headline: Nasdaq closes down roughly 1.4% to 1.6%, about triple the Dow's decline, ending the S&P 500's three-day winning streak
items.why: The damage was concentrated in tech and growth while about 81% of S&P 500 stocks advanced, so this was a rotation out of high-valuation leaders, not broad selling.
